host-setup.mode: Preview display, compaction and configuration guidance; --apply connects only the Claude display. Permissions are suggestions only.

permissions.mode: Print optional, command-scoped host permission suggestions. Writes no permission settings.

host-observe.usage: host-observe --host claude|codex --session id --data native-event.json --observed-at receive-time [--root project]
host-observe.mode: Record one fresh native context or compaction event forwarded by a connected host integration.

workspace-open.mode: lazily allocate bounded private scratch for the active task; no host temp/cache changes

workspace-write.mode: write a new bounded scratch file from {name,content}; existing files are never overwritten

workspace-promote.mode: intentionally retain bounded evidence from {name,purpose}; never promote secrets or transcripts

workspace-release.mode: release the current owner operation; task completion cleans disposable scratch when no other owner is active

workspace-clean.mode: reclaim closed or stale storage; open operations are retained until stale

state-clean.mode: preview session directories idle for 14 days with no lock or open workspace; --apply removes them; shared records are only reported

grounded-context.mode: Read-only citation composition; no task-state changes or command execution.

worker-status.mode: shared task-tree reservations and host observations; no dispatch

task-feature.mode: explicit evaluation classification only; normal delivery uses runtime observations and leaves missing evidence unknown

task-features.mode: all feature outcomes, provenance, missing evidence and stale-source markers

telemetry-capture.mode: explicit private immutable report retention; eight captures / 64 KiB; no automatic eviction

telemetry-forget.mode: explicitly remove one retained report; ordinary CLI telemetry still applies

telemetry-report.mode: bounded retained observation counts, loss reports and storage limits; no semantic or native execution claims

task-offer.usage: task-offer --session id --action review|delegate|compact --scope scope --benefit benefit --evidence evidence-id [--data observations.json] [--prior-authorization evidence-id]
task-offer.mode: evaluate and record a recommendation; no dispatch

task-decision.mode: record an explicit scoped user decision; no action execution

task-action-check.mode: revalidate source, approval, policy, support and capacity; no dispatch

task-start.usage: task-start --session id --task stable-id (--goal "outcome" | --plan id [--take-over]) [--stage implement] [--file src/path] [--repository relative/repo ...] [--contract contract.json]
task-start.mode: bind task identity and optional selected repository roots within the workspace; route guidance and snapshot selected Git worktrees

task-adopt.mode: copy an earlier session's unfinished task and checkpoint into this session and bind it; the earlier session is unchanged and no authorization is renewed

task-decide.usage: task-decide --session id --decision "what was decided" --by user|agent [--why "reason"] [--rejected "alternative" ...] [--supersedes d1] [--root project]
task-decide.mode: record a decision on the session's bound task; it is shown when the task resumes after compaction or in another session. A user decision records what the user said; it grants no authorization

task-step.usage: task-step --session id --stage verify --target acceptance:id --approach bounded-check --evidence evidence-id --outcome passed --result "observed result" --next "next step" [--acceptance-evidence ledger.json --expected-task-contract digest --expected-evidence-digest digest] [--complete]
task-step.mode: agent-declared semantic receipt, bounded continuation and next-step advice; no action dispatch

plan.mode: read-only: one plan as its Markdown view (JSON with --json), the plans linking a reference, or every plan's summary

plan-create.mode: create a local work plan; references are opaque and nothing is read from a tracker

plan-update.usage: plan-update --plan id --expected-revision N --data changes.json [--session id] [--take-over] [--root project]
plan-update.mode: revision-fenced change; a task another session holds changes only with --take-over

plan-envelope.mode: read-only: the task's goal, acceptance, owned scope, dependency results, parent checkpoint reference and latest decisions; --brief emits the worker brief

plan-assign.mode: claim a ready task that owns paths for a worker session of this session, in isolated worktrees below .craft/worktrees/<plan>/<task>-<attempt>/ on branch craft/<plan>/<task>-<attempt> unless --shared; refused at efficiency.delegation.maxWorkers or when a running task owns intersecting paths; no worker is started

plan-integrate.usage: plan-integrate --plan id --task task-id --session id [--escalate --reason text | --discard] [--root project]
plan-integrate.mode: merge a completed worktree task into the coordinator checkout when it merges cleanly (one merge commit per repository, nothing pushed); on conflicts the task runs again in this session to resolve them; --escalate hands it to the user, --discard returns it to pending

settings.usage: settings [--root project] [--organization organization.json] [--preferences user.json] [--data task-overrides.json] [--session id --facts worker-observations.json]
settings.mode: effective settings, value origins, applied controls and private state location; no action dispatch

config.usage: config [--root project] [--explain] [--field routing] [--organization organization.json] [--preferences user.json] [--json] | config [--root project] [--organization organization.json] --sync [--apply]
config.mode: Without --sync --apply, read-only: the organization, user and project layers the settings come from and each value one layer set over another. With --explain, every effective value with its layer and what it hid; --field keeps one field and what lies beneath it. A layer file that cannot be read or is invalid is an error naming the file. Where the machine has no organization file, a committed .craft/organization.json is the organization layer; where it has one, the pin is compared with it. --sync previews copying the machine's organization file to .craft/organization.json, so CI and teammates without it get the same layer; --apply writes it.

standards.mode: Without files, list declared standards. With --propose, list standards the project's existing convention files support, ready to copy into the configuration; nothing is written. With --file or --commit-message, run the deterministic anchor checks the hooks run; exits 2 when a standard is not met.

anchors.mode: Without --search, list the project's and Craft's anchors; with it, search the embedded catalog too by id, title, category or role. Each name shows the source it resolves to.

check.usage: check [--root project] [--stage step|commit|pr|ci] [--base ref | --file path ... | --all] [--session id] | check [--root project] --install-hook [--apply] | check [--root project] --ci-snippet github|gitlab
check.mode: Run the project's declared checks (modules[].checks, standards[].run) for the uncommitted changes (with --base, also the files committed since the ref's merge base with HEAD), the named files or, with --all, every declaration. A project below the top of its checkout reads its own folder; a workspace root reads each member repository. Commands start without a shell, each within its time bound. Checks of the stage (default commit) and earlier run; later ones are listed as left to their stage. Exits 1 when a check did not pass. --install-hook previews a Git pre-commit hook running the commit stage and writes it with --apply; where a hook manager (husky, lefthook, pre-commit), core.hooksPath or another hook owns pre-commit it prints the line to add and writes nothing. --ci-snippet prints a GitHub Actions or GitLab CI job that installs this Craft release and runs the ci stage since the target branch.

doctor.mode: Read-only unless asked: whether each host would run Craft for this project, from its install records, settings and Craft's hook telemetry. Writes nothing to host configuration or task state (only its own command telemetry) and starts nothing; only --deny-secret-files writes, merging Claude's secret-file deny rules into .claude/settings.local.json and keeping its other keys and rules. Exits 1 when an enabled package cannot run (missing or altered bundled runtime).

context-report.mode: selected guidance accounting; repeat --bundle for verified separately installed packages; no cache discovery or resource loading

locate.usage: locate --root project --term Foo --term Bar [--path src] [--session id --task task-id] [--max-output-bytes 32768]
locate.data: Alternatively --data request.json: terms or independent requests {id,term,dependsOn}, paths, maxFiles, maxMatches, maxBytes, maxOutputBytes
locate.mode: bounded literal scan; optional local reuse receipts

checkpoint-save.usage: checkpoint-save --root project --session id [--task task-id] [--repository relative/repo ...] --data handoff.json

acceptance-view.usage: acceptance-view --view qa|product|architecture --contract contract.json --acceptance-evidence ledger.json --current-kind repository|environment [--current-identity id] [--probes probes.json (qa)] [--focus focus.json (product, architecture)] [--blockers]
acceptance-view.mode: read-only reader view of supplied contract, evidence and probes; executes nothing and writes no task state

ticket.usage: ticket --ticket url-or-key --criteria clear|unclear|missing [--questions n] [--label name ...] [--path file ...] [--affects schema|config|state|hooks|api ...] [--host name] [--session id] [--root project] | ticket --ticket url-or-key --accept plan|direct --session id
ticket.mode: Decide how work that starts from a ticket is delivered: direct (one module, no contract change, clear acceptance criteria), plan first (several modules, a contract change, or unclear criteria) or ask (open questions). Prints the line for the user and the agent's next step on this host. With --accept, keep the user's choice for the session; a planned change ends with a review offer. No model call; nothing else is written.
